                    ### Question
                    A healthy 31-year-old woman comes to the physician because she is trying to conceive. She is currently timing the frequency of intercourse with at-home ovulation test kits. An increase in the levels of which of the following is the best indicator that ovulation has occurred?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Estrogen
opb. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
opc. Follicle stimulating hormone
opd. Progesterone
ope. Luteinizing hormone

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The best indicator that ovulation has occurred is the surge in Luteinizing hormone levels, which triggers ovulation. Progesterone rises after ovulation to prepare the uterus for potential pregnancy. Estrogen peaks just before ovulation, promoting the LH surge. Evidence supports the interaction between Estrogens and Luteinizing Hormone, and Progesterone's role in the uterus, aligning with the consensus on ovulation indicators.
